old: 丼[どん]
new: 丼[どんぶり]
why: Standalone 丼 is read どんぶり; どん occurs only in compounds (牛丼 ぎゅうどん).

old: don
new: donburi
why: Follows the reading fix.

new: In dish names it is ～どん: 牛丼 gyūdon, 親子丼 oyakodon, 天丼 tendon, かつ丼 katsudon.
why: Explain where it is read どん.

old: 辛[から]さはどうしますか
new: 辛[から]さはどうなさいますか
why: Staff speak in keigo: どうなさいますか (or いかがなさいますか); どうしますか is how a customer talks.

old: karasa wa dō shimasu ka
new: karasa wa dō nasaimasu ka
why: Follows the ruby.

new: からさはどうなさいますか
why: TTS may read 辛さ as つらさ; a kana override removes the risk.

new: からくないものはありますか
why: TTS may read 辛くない as つらくない; the override is harmless.

new: からくしないでください
why: TTS may read 辛く as つらく; the override is harmless.

old: パスポートはこれです
new: パスポートです
why: パスポートはこれです sounds like an answer to "which one is the passport?". When handing over a passport people say "(はい、)パスポートです".

old: pasupōto wa kore desu
new: pasupōto desu
why: Follows the ruby.

old: Usually needs an extra ticket.
new: JR and some private lines (Odakyu Romancecar, Tobu, Seibu, Kintetsu) need an extra 特急券 ticket; many private lines (Keio, Keikyu, Tokyu, Hankyu, Keihan) run 特急 at no extra charge.
why: "Usually needs an extra ticket" is true for JR, but on many private lines 特急 has no surcharge.

old: (before eating) Enjoy your meal / thank you
new: (before eating) Thank you for the food - I'm starting
why: いただきます is said by the person eating; it is not a wish of "enjoy your meal" to others.

new: Not "enjoy your meal" to others, but a formula said by the person eating.
why: Explains the translation.

old: What will you drink?
new: Anything to drink?
why: お飲み物はいかがですか means "Would you like something to drink?"; "What will you drink?" would be お飲み物は何になさいますか.

old: Do you have an insurance policy?
new: Do you have health insurance (a policy)?
why: 保険証 is the Japanese health insurance card.

new: 保険証 is the Japanese health insurance card; tourists don't have one. Reply: 海外旅行保険に入っています - and show your policy.
why: Link to family.insurance, otherwise it is unclear what to answer.

new: Number + 階: 1 いっかい, 3 さんがい, 6 ろっかい, 8 はっかい, 10 じゅっかい; 何階 なんがい. 地下1階 (ちか いっかい) = B1.
why: The romaji 〇-kai hides the sound changes, and those are exactly what people fail to recognise by ear.

new: Number + 階: 1 いっかい, 3 さんがい, 6 ろっかい, 8 はっかい, 10 じゅっかい. 地下 (ちか) - basement.
why: Sound changes of the counter 階.

new: Number + か月: 1 いっかげつ, 3 さんかげつ, 6 ろっかげつ, 10 じゅっかげつ; 1年 いちねん. 保証なし - no warranty.
why: Typical used-goods warranty periods (1/3/6 months) are pronounced with sound changes.

new: Often politer: おいくつですか (oikutsu desu ka). Reply: 〇歳です (〇-sai desu): 1 いっさい, 8 はっさい, 10 じゅっさい.
why: Staff and doctors often ask おいくつですか; the family needs an answer with the child's age.

new: Child ticket (小児, half price): ages 6-12 (primary school). Under 6: free (up to two children per adult) unless the child needs a separate reserved seat.
why: JR rules for children - without them people buy an extra ticket or fail to buy a needed one.

new: JR timetables more often say 土休日 (どきゅうじつ) - Sat, Sun and holidays; 平日 (へいじつ) - weekdays.
why: Departure boards and JR timetables show 土休日, not 土日祝.

new: On labels: 乳成分 (にゅうせいぶん) or 乳.
why: Allergen lists on packaging write 乳成分.

old: It was very delicious
new: It was delicious
why: The Japanese has no "very" (とても).

old: Where is a children's doctor?
new: Where is pediatrics (a children's doctor)?
why: 小児科 is a pediatric department/clinic.

old: I lost the ticket (masculine verb form only)
new: I lost the ticket (masculine/feminine verb forms)
why: A family is travelling: a woman needs the phrase too.

old: I rode past my stop (masculine verb form only)
new: I rode past my stop (masculine/feminine verb forms)
why: Grammatical gender.

old: I left the key in the room (masculine verb form only)
new: I left the key in the room (masculine/feminine verb forms)
why: Grammatical gender.

old: I hurt myself / got injured (masculine verb forms only)
new: I hurt myself / got injured (masculine/feminine verb forms)
why: Grammatical gender.

old: I lost my wallet (masculine verb form only)
new: I lost my wallet (masculine/feminine verb forms)
why: Grammatical gender.

old: I lost my phone (masculine verb form only)
new: I lost my phone (masculine/feminine verb forms)
why: Grammatical gender.

old: I'm lost. I need to get here. (masculine verb form only)
new: I'm lost. I need to get here. (masculine/feminine verb forms)
why: Grammatical gender.

old: お支払[しはら]い方法[ほうほう]は
new: お支払[しはら]い方法[ほうほう]は？
why: The phrase breaks off at は - without ？ it is not clear that it is a question (PLAN 4.9 had the mark).

old: oshiharai hōhō wa
new: oshiharai hōhō wa?
why: Follows the ruby.

old: Reply: はい.
new: Reply: はい. More common in electronics shops; variant: お支払い回数は？ ("In how many payments?") → 一括で (ikkatsu de).
why: Convenience stores hardly ever ask this; camera and watch shops ask it all the time.

old: For a child at sushi bars.
new: For a child at sushi bars. Staff say さび抜き (sabinuki).
why: Recognition by ear.

new: Ordinary over-the-counter medicine is easier to find at a ドラッグストア (doraggusutoa).
why: A tourist needs a drugstore more than a prescription pharmacy 薬局.

old: Dakuten (voicing: か→が) and handakuten (は→ぱ). (the term 'handakuten' was written in Latin script inside the Cyrillic text)
new: Dakuten (voicing: か→が) and handakuten (は→ぱ). (both terms in Cyrillic script)
why: A Latin-script term in the middle of Cyrillic text.
